result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.generate_stochastic_block_model()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Generate a graph from a stochastic block model (SBM). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L6261-L6379){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.generate_stochastic_block_model( sizes, p_matrix, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Stochastic block model](/assets/graphs/generate-stochastic-block-model.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three stochastic block models with two blocks of four nodes, block one in the accent color on the left and block two in teal on the right, with edge probability 0.9 inside a block and 0, 0.1, and 0.5 between blocks. Both blocks come out fully connected in every panel while the plain cross-block edges grow from none to 2 to 7, blurring the split." width="100%"} Creates a graph with nodes divided into blocks of the given sizes, where edges are added independently with probabilities specified by the block probability matrix. For every pair of distinct nodes, the model looks up the blocks the two nodes belong to and adds an edge with the probability given for that pair of blocks. Making the within-block probabilities (the diagonal of the matrix) higher than the between-block ones produces graphs with planted communities; the reverse produces bipartite-like or "disassortative" structure. Self-loops are never created. Because the true block of every node is known, SBMs are the standard benchmark for: - testing community detection algorithms, by checking whether they recover the planted blocks - exploring how detectability changes as the between-block probability approaches the within-block one - generating synthetic networks with group structure, e.g. social groups or modules This method doesn't use or modify the graph it is called on (other than recording the step); it returns an entirely new, undirected `Graph`, even when called on a directed graph. Nodes are labelled `"0"`, `"1"`, ... consecutively across blocks: the first `sizes[0]` labels belong to block `0`, the next `sizes[1]` to block `1`, and so on. Block membership is not stored as a node attribute, so derive it from the labels and `sizes=` if you need it. Every pair of nodes is checked, so the running time grows as the square of the total number of nodes. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [sizes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of block sizes (number of nodes in each block). The number of entries, `k`, is the number of blocks, and the total number of nodes is `sum(sizes)`. An empty list gives an empty graph. [p_matrix]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Flat row-major `k x k` probability matrix, where `k = len(sizes)`, so it must have exactly `k * k` entries, each in `[0.0, 1.0]`. Entry `p_matrix[i*k + j]` is the edge probability between blocks `i` and `j`; for two blocks this is `[p_00, p_01, p_10, p_11]`. Since the graph is undirected, only the entries with `i <= j` (the diagonal and upper triangle) are used and the lower-triangle entries are ignored, so pass a symmetric matrix to avoid surprises. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same `sizes=` and `p_matrix=` always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the result differs on every call. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new undirected graph generated from the SBM. The original graph is unchanged. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `p_matrix=` doesn't have exactly `len(sizes) ** 2` entries, or if any probability is outside `[0.0, 1.0]`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two blocks of ten nodes, densely connected inside (`0.8`) and sparsely between (`0.05`). Labels `"0"` to `"9"` form block `0` and `"10"` to `"19"` block `1`, so counting edges by block shows nearly all of them falling inside the blocks: ::: {#c9af2a75 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().generate_stochastic_block_model( sizes=[10, 10], p_matrix=[0.8, 0.05, 0.05, 0.8], seed=23 ) def block(nid): return 0 if int(graph.get_label_from_id(nid)) < 10 else 1 within = sum(block(s) == block(t) for _, s, t in graph.get_edges_as_tuples()) graph.count_edges(), within, graph.count_edges() - within ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (82, 76, 6) ``` ::: ::: A community detection algorithm should recover the planted blocks. Louvain assigns the first ten labels to one community and the last ten to another: ::: {#21aaa858 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} communities = graph.cmty_louvain(return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): communities[nid] for nid in sorted(communities)} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'0': 1, '1': 1, '2': 1, '3': 1, '4': 1, '5': 1, '6': 1, '7': 1, '8': 1, '9': 1, '10': 0, '11': 0, '12': 0, '13': 0, '14': 0, '15': 0, '16': 0, '17': 0, '18': 0, '19': 0} ``` ::: ::: With probability `1.0` inside blocks and `0.0` between them, the result is a set of disjoint cliques, which makes the labelling easy to see -- a triangle on `"0"`, `"1"`, `"2"` and a single edge between `"3"` and `"4"`: ::: {#86a74aaa .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} cliques = ec.Graph().generate_stochastic_block_model( sizes=[3, 2], p_matrix=[1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0] ) cliques.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['0--1', '0--2', '1--2', '3--4'] ``` ::: :::
